newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - April 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - April 9.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Wednesday:
* The Dow Industrials rose late in the day, gaining 53.25 points to close at 6,609.16.
* CSX and Norfolk Southern detailed a plan to split up the assets of Conrail.
* Apple Computer and IBM plan to try and renegotiate licence fees for Apple's Macintosh operating system software.
* Germany's highest court ruled farmers have to repay $6 billion in debt the collective farms accrued during the Communist era.
* Advertising: Federal Communications Commission Chairman Reed Hundt is trying to keep hard liquor advertising off television.
* Roussel Uclaf said it stopped making RU 486, its unprofitable abortion pill. The patent rights to the product would be transferred to a newly formed company.
* Dow Jones and Microsoft formed a techology and marketing alliance, in a bid to revive Dow's Telerate, which was recently renamed Dow Jones Markets.
* Polo Ralph Lauren plans an initial public offering it expects will generate around $600 million.
* A Presidential task force has agreed to create a code of conduct for apparel factories that U.S. companies use around the world.
* Federal investigators say little has been done to toughen gas pipeline standards.
* Ukraine's transition to a market economy is not going smoothly and diplomats and foreign executives blame official corruption.

* A romantic relationship between Cathy Minehan, president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston, and E. Gerald Corrigan, a partner at Goldman, Sachs & Co and a former president of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, has raised questions about a potential conflict of interest.
* Market place: Volume and prices of Alex. Brown shares and options soared before its announced merger with Bankers Trust. Now Tambrands is soaring in stock and options markets.
